capture.navigation_intent: Continue along the visible drivable road when permissible; obey visible signals and yield as needed. No map or future ego route is supplied.

hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional proposal, not verified executable. Road is a convex truncation of the side-street mouth and widening junction pavement, estimated from visible curbs, perspective and the MPV size prior; it includes the physical ego footprint and braking route. The rear-axle disk plus road uncertainty/safety margin may not fit the genuine narrow initial mouth. Do not enlarge this road to resolve that conflict. The retained following-car adverse envelope also threatens the stopped ego under disk inflation, so independent verification may reject this proposal. Initial speed is 2.72346 m/s; stopping by 1.2 s within 1.6 m is physically achievable with approximately 2.5–3 m/s² braking. No optimization or prefix simulation was performed. Excluded conditions include new entrants from the cross street, other sidewalk pedestrians entering the patch, and hidden traffic; their absence is explicitly conditional, not observed world safety.

premises.statement: Local two-second task is braking within this observed pavement patch, not crossing the junction. Adopt no new unmodelled entrant into this patch during [0,2]. Other visible cross-street vehicles and more distant sidewalk pedestrians remain outside it; no concealed or off-image traffic enters. The declared MPV, crossing pedestrians, corner scooter and following car are retained even where their sources extend outside this domain. These exclusions are falsifiable conditional assumptions, not claims that other traffic is absent.

Assume the visible silver MPV has length 4.8 m and width 1.85 m. Approximate rear-face apparent width, its oblique orientation and calibrated bearing support center roughly [8.5,3.8]. Transfer this approximate scale to pavement and pedestrian geometry; no certified ground plane is assumed.

Silver MPV continues its observed leftward turn with center x in [8.5,11], y in [3.8,7], yaw in [0.4,1.2], or brakes with center x in [8.5,9.5], y in [3.8,4.8], yaw in [0.4,0.8]. No reverse or turn back toward ego. Rectangles include the complete rotating body.

Three approaching crossing pedestrians walk toward decreasing x: adopted displacement 0–2.3 m, lateral displacement at most 0.3 m; adverse displacement 0–3.2 m and lateral displacement at most 1 m. No running. Umbrella pedestrian source additionally allows carried-umbrella width. Complete body extent is included in every source.

Corner scooter/rider waits or creeps at at most 0.5 m/s without entering farther inward than y=4.1 at its center; heading remains within 0.2 rad of the body hypothesis. Evidence-to-reference displacement is at most 0.003808 m. Rider and scooter fit the declared body envelope.

Rear car moves forward at 0–3 m/s with yaw within 0.1 rad and center lateral displacement at most 0.5 m. Adopted mode brakes with forward displacement at most 2 m; adverse mode continues with displacement at most 6 m. Evidence-to-reference displacement at most 0.074806 m. Its adverse approach is retained, not excluded by local scope.

anchors.rationale: Conditional ordinary full-size MPV body-length prior for the individually visible silver turning vehicle.
Conditional MPV body-width prior; apparent rear width and oblique pose provide approximate range support.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: The latest front image places the silver MPV left of the optical axis with a rear face several hundred pixels wide. A 1.85 m width at focal length about 1266 pixels suggests rear-face range of several metres, with oblique projection and half-body length placing its body center approximately 8.5 m forward and 3.8 m left. Visible pavement edges widen toward the junction; the left curb remains close beside the initial ego. The resulting convex patch is deliberately not widened to satisfy the disk model. Other native positions use calibrated bearings and perspective at this conditional scale, with explicit noncalibrated residuals.
